topics.topic: Concrete Python runtime artifact identified and compared by the required digest
questions: What concrete Python runtime artifact does the required digest identify and compare: a distribution archive, an executable, an installed runtime tree, or a constituent of the base image?

What concrete artifact does the required digest of “the Python version” identify and compare: a source archive, an interpreter distribution, an executable, a complete runtime tree, or a constituent of the base image?
What concrete Python runtime artifact must the required digest identify and compare: a distribution archive, an executable, the complete installed runtime tree, or a containing image constituent?

quotes:
1. A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with
   its digest: every Python package, direct or transitive, by the digest of
   its distribution file; the Python version; and the base image of VM
   Platform's Registry environment by its digest, which fixes the system
   libraries and the store's engine. Tools used only to build or test are not
   dependencies of the running instance.

1. Installing the release fails when the digest differs for any one
   dependency of each kind rule 1 names — a direct Python package, a
   transitive one, the Python version and the base image — and no instance
   of that release starts.

5. Rules 1–4 are kept by the release process and its installation, which
   Registry does not manage (00_product.md, Explicit exclusions): they make
   the release, name its dependencies and install them, and Registry's own
   code reads none of it (owner, 2026-11-24). This decision therefore
   declares no formal invariant of Registry: no note of a module and no
   check of Registry's code can show what the installation does, and one
   claimed here would be a false witness.
judgement.divergence: Different choices of digest subject make the installer accept or refuse different byte changes, but State 2 already requires the selected Python dependency to be identified exactly and a mismatch to prevent startup.
judgement.why: Choosing the concrete installable Python artifact and comparison representation is a release-process and deployment mechanism, while State 2 fixes the result that the selected exact runtime dependency is digested and a mismatch prevents that release from starting.
options: Digest a named Python distribution or source archive
Digest the installed Python executable
Digest a canonical complete installed runtime tree
Represent Python as a constituent fixed by the base-image digest
consequences: The deployment specification must identify one comparison subject unambiguously so every verifier reaches the same installation result while preserving the separate Python-version-and-digest obligation.

topics.topic: Scope of packages subject to exact-version and digest verification
questions: Does “a package the instance would import” mean a package imported on the verification path, every package reachable on any supported runtime path, or the complete declared direct-and-transitive dependency closure?
Does “any of them” cover every package named in the release list, including a package the instance would never import, or only the previously mentioned packages that the instance would import?

quotes:
1. A release names every dependency it runs with, at an exact version, with
   its digest: every Python package, direct or transitive, by the digest of
   its distribution file; the Python version; and the base image of VM
   Platform's Registry environment by its digest, which fixes the system
   libraries and the store's engine. Tools used only to build or test are not
   dependencies of the running instance.

2. A release whose list misses a package the instance would import, the
   Python version or the base image, or names any of them without an exact
   version or a digest, is not made.

3. After an installation that succeeded, the dependencies the running
   instance has are exactly the release's list, by name, version and
   digest, nothing more.
judgement.why: The rules cover every direct and transitive runtime package, including one imported only on a supported optional path, require each listed runtime dependency to have an exact version and digest, and require the successful installation's dependency set to equal the list exactly rather than limiting verification to packages imported while checks execute.
options: Only packages imported while release verification executes
Every package imported on any supported runtime path
The complete direct-and-transitive runtime dependency closure
Allow a named never-imported package without an exact version or digest
Require every listed runtime dependency to have an exact version and digest
Forbid dependencies outside the exact running dependency set
consequences: An optional runtime package cannot be omitted merely because release checks do not execute its path, and an unversioned or undigested package cannot be admitted as part of the release's running dependency list.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
State 2: decide required results and constraints, including necessary refusal precedence; carry test mechanisms, exact contracts and deployment procedures to their owners.
